subject.title: Feature Request: Session rotation/archive lifecycle event for cron job triggers

question: Should session archive/rotation automation be supported as a core Cron event schedule, as a plugin `session_end` workflow with a narrow missing SDK seam, or not as a new OpenClaw core surface?
rationale: Current main has the lifecycle hook primitive but not the requested Cron subscription or external-plugin agent-turn scheduling contract, and the permanent shape affects public Cron config, plugin API boundaries, archived transcript metadata, and security review.

options.title: Use plugin lifecycle plus narrow SDK seam
options.body: Bless plugin `session_end` as the session-boundary signal and add only the smallest SDK scheduling or event-dispatch capability external plugins need to run this workflow safely.

options.title: Add core Cron lifecycle schedules
options.body: Define `schedule.kind: event` for session archive/rotation in the Gateway protocol with scoped metadata, permissions, persistence, docs, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Keep it plugin-owned without new core work
options.body: If maintainers decide current plugin hooks already cover the use case, route the self-improving memory workflow to a ClawHub plugin and document the supported pattern.

recommendation.title: Use plugin lifecycle plus narrow SDK seam
recommendation.body: Bless plugin `session_end` as the session-boundary signal and add only the smallest SDK scheduling or event-dispatch capability external plugins need to run this workflow safely.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits at the hook/plugin SDK/core Cron boundary where this history shows the strongest recent hook and plugin-boundary work.
